clue.text: Most domestic trouble is unobtrusive

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
most of a word is all of it but its tail, so the final two letters of domestic are cut

explanation.surface: Most household rows are kept quiet rather than aired in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' trims DOMESTIC to DOMEST, and 'trouble' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person is retiring and unassuming, not pushing themselves forward.

clue.text: Various kinds of person entitled to a pension

definitions.text: kinds of person entitled to a pension
definitions.meaning: read as a description of who qualifies: a male if aged, three short words run together

explanation.surface: Different categories of people qualify for a retirement pension.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as MAN IF OLD, someone who gets a pension once old.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and varied, of several kinds.

clue.text: Ride a bit carelessly and get a wigging

indicators.note: doing something carelessly leaves it in a mess, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A careless horse rider gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A wigging is old British slang for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, close to a wigging or scolding.

clue.text: Rogue politician fell over

annotationWithheld.why: Rogue politician fell over (5), SCAMP: 'politician' gives MP but no reading of 'fell over' yields SCA or a reversal giving SCAMP; no blog parse found.

clue.text: Lad rejected gift, which is outrageous

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the lad's name is read backwards

parts.note: Alf is a typical boy's name, standing for any lad
a grant is money given, a gift

explanation.surface: A boy turns down a present, which shocks everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ALF into FLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant behaviour is glaringly offensive, so outrageous is a close synonym.

clue.text: Cooking a fowl means a dubious mathematical proposition

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: means are averages in statistics

explanation.surface: Roasting a chicken is said to be a questionable piece of maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges A FOWL into LAWOF.
explanation.definitionFit: The so-called law of averages is a popular but statistically shaky idea about chance evening out.

clue.text: State call includes study of cultivation

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for Georgia

indicators.note: includes means holds inside, so the word for study sits within the word for call

parts.note: to ring is to telephone, to call
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A state telephone call contains research into farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardening is the tending and growing of plants, a form of cultivation.

clue.text: In game play is a form of discrimination

indicators.note: play means movement or looseness, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: In sport, a certain way of playing is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges GAME and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people because of how old they are.

clue.text: Barley drink makes girl sit up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so both pieces are turned

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A drink of barley water brings a girl to sit upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link; in a down clue 'up' turns the girl's name and the verb together. The French word tisane first meant barley water before any herbal infusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion; barley water was its original sense.

clue.text: US state like a lake in Africa

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
as means like, in a comparison

explanation.surface: Something is compared with an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Nyasa is the old name for Lake Malawi in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasa is the older name of Lake Malawi, a great lake of Africa's Rift Valley.

clue.text: Peers slow to reform, lacking teeth

indicators.note: reform means to reshape, so the letters of the two words are made over

explanation.surface: The House of Lords is slow to change and so has no real bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' and 'reform' point to the House of Lords, but 'to reform' tells you to rearrange PEERS SLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking teeth has no power to enforce its will: it is impotent.

clue.text: Anti-abortion (or anti-operation) is increasing

parts.note: those opposed to abortion call themselves pro-life

indicators.note: an operation acts on something, here working the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Campaigners opposed to abortion, or to surgery generally, are multiplying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation', inside 'anti-operation', is the anagram signal: OR ANTI becomes RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is rapid growth in number, an increasing.

clue.text: Like asbestos, if backing censure

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the little word if is turned round

parts.note: a reproof is a rebuke, a censure

explanation.surface: Asbestos-style materials are criticised if supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos was prized because it will not burn, the property of being flame-resistant.

clue.text: Where to eat in Germany?

parts.note: reads like a request for a restaurant, but the German verb for eat is also the name of a city in the Ruhr

explanation.surface: A traveller asks for a good place to dine in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The German verb 'to eat' is spelt the same as the city of Essen.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a German industrial city whose name matches the German infinitive meaning to eat.

clue.text: Futile party?

parts.note: a phrase meaning wasted effort is read as if it described a political party that gets nowhere

explanation.surface: A political party that achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for fruitless effort begins with the name of Britain's Labour Party, so 'party' hints at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means toiling to no purpose, while its first word names a British political party.

clue.text: Contrived murder most foul

definitions.meaning: Hamlet's ghost calls his killing 'murder most foul'

explanation.surface: A forced, artificial plot about a terrible killing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ghost in Shakespeare's Hamlet says: 'Murder most foul, as in the best it is; But this most foul, strange and unnatural.'
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural means artificial or affected, and also monstrous, as Hamlet's ghost describes his murder.

clue.text: Drab end of brass instrument

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a trumpet is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A dull ending to a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab' looks like an adjective meaning dull; here it is an old noun for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab and strumpet are both old words for a prostitute.

clue.text: Spirit of fear Magna Carta conveys

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so the phrase carries the answer inside it

explanation.surface: The spirit of fear carried by the great charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveys' tells you the answer runs across feAR MAGNA Carta.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony, a distilled spirit.

clue.text: Inquisitor used terror to gain conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inquisitor used fear to force people to change their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges TERROR TO GAIN; the Inquisition sought religious conversions, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquisitor questions people closely, as an interrogator does.

clue.text: One writing notes to scratch a living?

definitions.text: One writing notes to scratch a living?

parts.words: One writing notes to scratch a living?
parts.note: a composer earning a meagre living is also, punningly, someone who scratches marks for a living

explanation.surface: A composer struggling to make ends meet.
explanation.walkthrough: To score is both to write music and to scratch or mark a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer writes musical scores, and to score is also to scratch lines.

clue.text: Indulged in sort of bad habit

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: use can mean a custom or habit

explanation.surface: Someone gave way to a kind of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indulged' stands for over-indulging in drink or drugs, and 'habit' is the old sense of use as custom; 'sort of' scrambles the three-letter word before 'in' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse drugs or drink is to overindulge in them.

clue.text: Rating in bed with navigator

indicators.note: the sailor's abbreviation is placed inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A sailor lies in his bunk beside a ship's navigator.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer who sailed to North America for England in 1497.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was a fifteenth-century explorer who crossed the Atlantic, a famous navigator.

clue.text: Drunken Argonauts in the pink

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Jason's sailors are tipsy and in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' looks like 'in good health' but means 'in a pink gin', whose colour comes from these bitters.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters are the ingredient that colours a pink gin, so they are what is in the pink.

clue.text: One's mood voiced on premature arousal?

definitions.text: One's mood voiced on premature arousal?

parts.words: One's mood voiced on premature arousal?
parts.note: someone woken too soon grumbles that it is so early, and that grumble sounds like a word for bad temper

explanation.surface: How you feel and speak when woken too early.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'it's early' shortened to 's early sounds like the bad-tempered word.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly means bad-tempered and gruff, the mood of someone woken too soon.

clue.text: Holds back from occurrence of poor weather during vacations

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: rests are breaks or holidays
rain is a spell of bad weather

explanation.surface: Bad weather on holiday keeps people indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or check something.

clue.text: Mature divinity writer

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the school subject of divinity
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An older author who writes on theology.
explanation.walkthrough: RI stands for Religious Instruction, the British school lesson also called divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become fully developed, to mature.

clue.text: Benefit swallowed by cost of a room that's odorous

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: rent is what one pays for lodging
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Welfare money disappears into the rent for a smelly room.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British informal name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means smelling strongly of something, hence odorous.

clue.text: Like Teresa — chemistry isn't the same without her

indicators.note: the letters left after removing a short word are changed in order, so the remainder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Teresa is the special ingredient that keeps the relationship's chemistry alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, E, R out of CHEMISTRY and rearrange CMISTY; St Teresa of Avila was a celebrated Christian mystic.
explanation.definitionFit: St Teresa of Avila had visions and wrote on prayer, the classic example of a mystic.
